description: Manipulate logical expressions and use logic for inference in propositional and predicate logic, including truth values, logical equivalence, translation between logical expressions and sentences, quantifiers including nested quantifiers, rules of inference, and validity of conclusions.

Perform basic operations on sets, functions, and sequences, including set terminology, power sets, Cartesian products, binary-bit subset representation, set operations and equality, function rules and operations including floor and ceiling functions, one-to-one, onto, and bijection properties, sequence formulas, finite sums, and special summations.
Analyze basic algorithms written in pseudocode and determine their complexities, including searching, sorting, greedy algorithms, growth of functions, and Big-O, Big-Omega, and Big-Theta estimates.

Discuss applications of modular arithmetic and analyze algorithms on integers, including integer division, congruence, pseudorandom-number and cryptology applications, base-b expansion, binary operations, modular exponentiation, prime numbers, prime factorization, greatest common divisors, least common multiples, and integer algorithms.

Use induction and recursive definitions to prove statements or describe objects, and write recursive algorithms using mathematical induction, strong induction, recursive definitions, structural induction, and recursive algorithms including mergesort. Distinguish between iterative and recursive algorithms.
Solve counting problems using basic counting principles, recurrence relations, and divide-and-conquer recurrence methods.

Analyze graph structures and shortest paths in weighted graphs, including graph models, special graph types, the handshaking theorem, bipartite graphs, incidence and adjacency matrices, graph isomorphism, connectivity, connected components, path counting, Euler and Hamilton paths and circuits, and running Dijkstra's algorithm to determine shortest paths and shortest distances.

Analyze tree structures and tree-based algorithms, including tree terminology, m-ary trees, binary search trees, decision trees, complexity of tree operations, prefix codes and Huffman coding, tree traversal with infix, prefix, and postfix notation, expression evaluation, depth-first and breadth-first search for spanning trees, and minimum spanning tree algorithms such as Prim and Kruskal.
